newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin will meet PM, but other meetings limited.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin will meet PM, but other meetings limited.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from pneumonia, will cut down his schedule this week to work on his annual report to parliament but will be seeing his prime minister, the Kremlin said on Monday.
Spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Itar-Tass news agency the 66-year-old president was expected to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday.
But other meetings would be limited because Yeltsin had not yet fully recovered from the pneumonia which laid him low on January 8.
Yeltsin, whose health has been watched nervously by foreign governments and investors alike, has visited the Kremlin only three times since then.
He had only been back in the seat of power for a fortnight after his recovery from major heart surgery in November.
Yeltsin will be working with his close aides on the annual report on the state of the nation, the equivalent of the U.S. president's state-of-the-union address, at a residence outside Moscow.
During their traditional Tuesday meeting, Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin will discuss the prime minister's trip to Switzerland last week, where he attended the World Economic Forum conference.
Chernomyrdin, Russia's constitutional number two, runs most of the state affairs during Yeltsin's illness but the Kremlin insists the president remains in overall control.
Yeltsin held talks with visiting French President Jacques Chirac on Sunday, his first meeting with a Western leader since the pneumonia struck.
Chirac told reporters he had talked for more than three hours with the Kremlin leader, and was very impressed with the speed of Yeltsin's recovery.
